title.zh: 卷六十五 表第三: 公主表
title.raw: 卷六十五 表第三: 公主表 Volume 65 Tables 3: Princesses

sentences.zh: 春秋之法，王姬下嫁書于策，以魯公同姓之國為之婚主故爾。

translations.literal: In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a king's daughter married down it was written in the chronicle, because the state of Lu, sharing the lord's surname, served as marriage host—hence this.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a royal daughter was given in marriage the event was entered in the chronicle because Lu, a state of the same surname as the Zhou king, acted as ceremonial marriage host.

sentences.zh: 古者，婦諱不出門，內言不出梱。

translations.literal: In antiquity a woman's tabooed name did not leave the door, and domestic talk did not pass beyond the threshold-curtain.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times a woman's personal name never left the household, and family matters were not spoken of beyond the inner quarters.

translations.literal: To list all princesses fully in biographies is not ritual-proper.
translations.idiomatic: Recording every princess at length in biographical chapters was not proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 然遼國專任外戚，公主多見紀、傳間，不得不表見之。

translations.literal: Yet the Liao state relied exclusively on maternal kin, and princesses often appear between annals and biographies; one cannot but set them forth in a table.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Liao gave sole weight to maternal kin, and princesses appear so often in annals and biographies that they must be set out here in tabular form.

sentences.zh: 禮，男女異長，不當與皇子同列，別為公主附表。

translations.literal: By rites men and women differ in seniority; they ought not share a column with imperial sons—a separate appended table for princesses.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual propriety men and women follow different lines of seniority; princesses should not be listed with imperial sons, so they are given this separate appended table.

translations.literal: Imperial Son-in-law Tabuye was killed for involvement in Prince Zhaohuai's affair; his younger brother Eduwo wished to force marriage to the princess, but the princess detested Eduwo as a partisan of Yixin. Before long Eduwo was executed for his crimes. Tianzuo was young and Yixin held power; the princess constantly sought to save and restore order, and in the end Yixin was executed.

cells.content: 公主從天祚出奔。明年，攻應州，留公主守輜重。金人圍之，公主奔行在所，天祚潛遁，為金人所獲。

translations.literal: The princess followed Tianzuo in flight. The next year, attacking Ying Prefecture, he left the princess to guard the baggage train. Jin troops surrounded them; the princess fled to the traveling court, Tianzuo slipped away secretly, and was captured by Jin.

cells.content: 大康八年，以駙馬都尉蕭酬斡得罪，離之。大安初，改適蕭特末。為都統，與金人戰，敗于石輦鐸，被擒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dakang, because Imperial Son-in-law Xiao Chouwo was punished, she divorced him. At the beginning of Da'an she remarried Xiao Temo. As commander-in-chief he fought Jin and was defeated at Shinian Duo and captured.

cells.content: 幼遭乙辛之難，與兄天祚俱養于蕭懷忠家。後李氏進挾穀歌，文帝感悟，召還宮。

translations.literal: In youth she suffered Yixin's persecution and, with her brother Tianzuo, was raised in Xiao Huaizhong's household. Later Lady Li advanced with Jia Guge; Emperor Wen was moved and summoned them back to the palace.

cells.content: 俱為金人所獲。俱為金人所獲 按金史七四宗望傳，天祚女為金人所俘者有骨欲、餘里衍，斡里衍、大奧野、次奧野，惟長女乘軍亂逃去。餘里衍即余里衍。

translations.literal: All captured by Jin—per Jin History, Biography 74 Zongwang, among Tianzuo's daughters captured by Jin were Guyü, Yuliyan, Woliyan, Da'aoye, and Ci'aoye; only the eldest escaped during the army turmoil. Yuliyan is Yuliyan.
